To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CP-asymmetry in the effective potential and in the chargino sector is sufficient to create a baryon excess of the order of 10^-2.
the electroweak beryogenesis in the SUSY model with the singlet is possible and the chargino contribution is dominant.
in a supersymmetric model with a gauge-singlet scalar field a baryon excess can be created in the hot electroweak plasma via the electroweak sphaleron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1.
the generation of the observed baryon asymetry in the Universe by a mechanism called baryogenesis via a strongly first order EWPT.
two aspects of electroweak banyogenesis in the MSSM with a gauge singet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a strong first order EWPT in a SUSY theory with a singlet is not sufficient to generate the baryon asymetry of the universe.
the baryon asymmetries generated in the hot phase by the CP-violating source terms are of the order of a few times 10^-8.
the baryon asymetry of the Universe is created by CP-violating charginos in a first order EWPT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the MSSM the baryon asymetry is not produced in the hot phase but in the bubble wall.
in the MSSM with a singlet, CP-violating phases in the chargino mass matrix are crucial in generating a baryon number.
a baryon number of about 10^{-10} can be generated in the SUSY singlet model, which is sufficient to explain the observed baryon asymmetries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charginos are the most efficient CP-violating source in the bubble wall.
in the SUSY models considered here a large baryon asymetry can be generated in a region in the parameter space where the EWPT is first order and the sphaleron rate is large, in contrast to the MSSM.
the baryon asymetry is generated at a much lower temperature than the EWPT, which is a generic feature of SUSY models.
